observations: Two photos show a blue plastic water drum/barrel with a screw/plug cap on top.
The side text appears to include a capacity marking that looks like '210' and '10.2kg' (exact wording not fully clear).
The drum looks empty (no visible water inside).
No visible cracks/holes are obvious from these photos, but the surface has scuffs/marks.

identity.kind: plastic water drum / water storage barrel

claims.claim: Empty plastic water drum for water
claims.evidence: Photos 0-1 show an empty-looking blue plastic water drum with a top cap; no water is visible.

risks.risk: Capacity/size may not match what you need (capacity marking is not fully readable).
risks.proof: Ask for a clear close-up photo of the capacity/weight marking on the drum side (the full text/number).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used plastic water drum (worst-case size uncertainty).

risks.risk: Leak risk: drum may not be watertight (cap seal/gasket condition not shown).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the cap being tightened plus a leak test (fill to near top and show no dripping for a few minutes).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed watertight (worst case for water storage).

risks.risk: Condition risk: hidden cracks/warping or pinholes may exist (photos only show exterior).
risks.proof: Ask for photos of the bottom and around the rim/edges, plus a close-up of any scuffed areas.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used with possible wear (worst case: may need minor repair).

risks.risk: Cap/parts completeness: the top cap may be missing a gasket or may not fit properly.
risks.proof: Ask for a close-up photo of the cap underside/gasket and the cap threads.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as cap present but seal condition unknown (worst case: may not seal well).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the full capacity marking on the drum side (so we know the exact size).
Close-up of the top cap and any gasket/seal (underside + threads).
Photo of the bottom of the drum (entire base).
Short video showing the drum filled briefly and demonstrating no leaks/drips after tightening the cap.
response.reason: It’s clearly a used plastic water drum, but the exact capacity and watertight condition (cap seal/gasket and any hidden leaks) aren’t verifiable from these photos. Those factors strongly affect the price, so we need the key close-ups/leak proof before pricing.
